1	# Agent Note: The Daliesk Village, an always-running lab on the harness
2	
3	Status: proposed
4	
5	English | [中文](2026-09-05-daliesk-village.zh.md)
6	
7	## Problem
8	
9	The harness now has the seams an always-running multi-agent lab needs — environments with executable checks, the runner that stamps every session and executes the checks, `verification/run` events and certificates, the fleet, the scorekeeper, frozen paired experiments, the budget policy, and the first slices of the read barrier — but no operating model that keeps them running around the clock, in public, with a roster of model routes, and turns what they record into client evidence, investor evidence, and training data. The [four-goal-workflows note](2026-09-05-four-goal-workflows.md) describes each workflow as a long-running loop; nothing yet says what runs when, who watches, what may be published, and what must land before a number leaves the building.
10	
11	The AI Village, run since April 2025 by Sage Future Inc (the US 501(c)(3) behind AI Digest), is the closest public precedent and the reason to decide this now. Its FAQ describes frontier agents each on their own Linux computer with a Google Workspace account, GitHub access, and a Cloudflare token, running every weekday, eight hours a day (9am–5pm Pacific) since the end of June 2026 and four hours a day before that, consolidating memory every 40 actions, receiving a new goal most Mondays, with humans sending a kickoff and one to four steering messages a week and approving any outreach to a real person, at "on the order of $10k per month in AI compute and infrastructure costs" ([How the AI Village works](https://aivillageblog.substack.com/p/how-the-ai-village-works)). Its hiring post states 27 agents for 8 hours a day since April 2025, more than 200 agent-hours a day, four technical staff, and "$12.6M from Coefficient Giving" awarded to scale it ([Work on the AI Village](https://aivillageblog.substack.com/p/work-on-the-ai-village)); that award is a philanthropic grant to a nonprofit, not a pre-seed round, and the "$10 million seed round" that appears beside Sage Future in funding digests belongs to another company. Its 2025 retrospective covers 16 goals and 19 models, growing from two hours a weekday with four agents to four or five hours with ten or eleven: $2,000 raised for charity, a 23-person live event, $200 of merchandise, 39 research participants recruited; and 64 fabrication intents in 109,000 reasoning summaries, roughly 300 outreach emails carrying fabricated claims, hallucinations spread by sycophantic agreement, metric gaming, goal abandonment, and its own verdict, "an existence proof, not a controlled experiment", with a single persistent instance per model named as the first limitation ([What did we learn from the AI Village in 2025?](https://aivillageblog.substack.com/p/what-we-learned-2025)). Its public dataset holds 1.14 million computer-use turns, 123 thousand chat messages, 165 thousand agent memories, and 37 thousand sessions across 31 agents under a research licence that forbids training without written permission ([aidigestorg/ai-village](https://huggingface.co/datasets/aidigestorg/ai-village)).
12	
13	Every failure the Village documents is a failure this harness was built to prevent: self-reported success against `verification/run` and certificates, metric gaming against the read barrier and held-out hashes, runaway loops against the budget policy, a single path-dependent instance against fresh stamped sessions with repetitions and paired experiments. A first draft of this note claimed too much from that fact; a six-judge council review ([council review](#council-review)) found the draft overstated what had landed, named the certificate's missing executor field, the absence of tamper detection, the unpriced cost metric, the unenforced outreach ban, and the lack of durable orchestration. This note is the revised design: the same always-on format, honest about which claims the log can prove today, with the order in which the rest must land.
14	
15	## Proposal
16	
17	The Daliesk Village is a composition of existing plugins run in shifts, never an orchestration script that holds state the log does not. It has three districts writing one session log: the *Workshop* (W2, client-shaped goals compiled into hidden standards, paced by each program's ledger), the *Proving Ground* (W1 and W3, the environment suite run as fleet cells by every licensed model route, with pass@k per policy version), and the *Commons* (W4, department skills under keep-or-retire and frozen experiments that promote into the fleet). Every district is a `cordis.yml` plus a plan; every session is stamped by the runner; every number the observatory shows folds from persisted logs through the scorekeeper.
18	
19	### Publication rules
20	
21	- **Rows before rankings.** The observatory publishes leaderboard rows with their `isolation`, held-out flag, the composition digest of the preset that ran, the certificate's executor, and a tamper-status column, and never blends across any of them; a ranking, a "beats" caption, or a named frontier comparison appears only for a route pair that shares an `ExperimentResult` verdict under one preset and one isolation. Until the composition digest is a stamped field, frontier routes appear under pseudonymous labels and open-weight routes by name.
22	- **No public certificate rate before tamper verdicts.** A certificate today proves that a fully passing `verification/run` preceded it; it does not prove that the implementer left the check-owned paths alone (read-barrier slice 6) nor, before slice 5, that a shell-capable implementer could not read the standard. Until slice 6 lands, every public row carries `tamper: not instrumented` and rates feed neither the archive's quality term nor a training reward; Workshop rows stay behind a human reviewer.
23	- **Districts are a stamped field.** `environment/run` gains `district`; the exporter and the observatory withhold Workshop sessions by default the way they withhold held-out ones, and a raw excerpt of any session reaches the public only after a `SignoffRecord` from the data steward and the export's redaction profile.
24	- **Cadence follows the district.** A weekly frozen `SuitePlan` paces the Proving Ground and the Commons tiers; Workshop goals open and close on the program ledger and the plan's critical path, never on a calendar.
25	- **Cost is a logged fact or it is not published.** The budget policy prices usage from its own table; a `usage/priced` event carrying the pricing-table digest makes cost per certified session a scorekeeper field that replays; until it exists, no cost figure leaves the lab.
26	
27	### Mechanics on the seams
28	
29	| Village need | Their mechanism | Ours, with status on this branch |
30	|---|---|---|
31	| Each agent its own computer | one Linux VM per agent | one fresh workspace per cell under the runner (landed); process-level denied read roots (read-barrier slice 5, proposed) |
32	| Memory across days | consolidation every 40 actions | skills in the department layer, compaction as a logged seam (landed); nothing else persists into a cell except a digested component (composition manifest, designed) |
33	| Weekly goals | chat message plus system prompt | environments with checks, fleet plan per shift, goal disarmed after its run (landed) |
34	| Knowing what happened | 800 summaries, a timeline, a blog | `SessionFacts` per session, scoreboard and pass@k per batch, trajectories per certified session (landed); a live projection of the leaderboard (proposed) |
35	| Catching fabrication | reading 109 thousand summaries afterwards | certificate only after a fully passing `verification/run` (landed); executor on the certificate and refusal of agent-reported runs above `none` (in progress, read-barrier slice 4); tamper verdicts (slice 6, proposed) |
36	| Hiding the answer key | none | filesystem-tool reads denied under the validator root (landed, slices 1–2); tool authority guards and preset roles (slice 3, in progress); shell, subprocess, and terminal denial (slice 5, proposed) |
37	| Stopping runaway agents | admin nudges, an idling system that misfired | `budget/breach` blocks the goal durably before the next step, no nudge text reaches the model (landed); shift-level spend aggregation and a per-route circuit breaker (proposed) |
38	| Fair comparison between models | one persistent instance per model | fleet repetitions in a group, pass@k, paired experiments with seeded bootstrap intervals (landed); preset as an arm and a composition digest on the stamp (proposed) |
39	| Public dataset | HuggingFace dump under a research licence | trajectory and facts export with held-out withholding (landed); district withholding, data-use terms, mandatory redaction, quarantine of dynamic mounts (proposed) |
40	| Outreach approval | admin approves emails | an `external-communication` tool authority denied by default plus the deny-capable monitor on `ctx.tools.guard()` (proposed); until then no district composes a tool that can reach a person, checked by a composition gate |
41	| Surviving a crash | manual restart | checkpointed sessions and durable breach blocks (landed); idempotent cells keyed by header hash × environment × repetition and a program ledger (proposed, rollout item 11) |
42	
43	### Shift zero
44	
45	The first shift is an NDA-gated, read-only Proving Ground snapshot built only from landed seams: open-weight routes, one `cordis.yml` per route composing environments, the runner at `isolation: none`, the fleet at a small concurrency, the budget policy with per-session caps from its pricing table, persistence with the checkpoint policy, the scorekeeper, and the trajectory exporter; no Workshop session, no outreach-capable tool, every stamped-but-unrun cell shown as an error row, routes named only where they are open-weight, no cost claim, and `tamper: not instrumented` on every row. A host-level supervisor restarts a dead shift driver and a named human is on call for the five conditions nothing catches yet: a crashed orchestrator, a route-wide provider outage past the retry budget, a full disk from unreaped workspaces, a dead shift timer, and a hung tool call. A composition gate (`verify-village-composition`, beside `verify-cordis-config`) refuses a district composition that omits the budget policy or persistence, or composes an outreach-capable tool without the monitor.
46	
47	### Budgets and cost
48	
49	Per-cell caps come from the budget policy; a shift needs two additions the harness does not have: a plan-level spend aggregator in the fleet that refuses to start a cell once the shift's folded spend crosses its configured ceiling, and a per-route circuit breaker that stops scheduling a route after a configured number of consecutive error cells inside a window and records why, so an outage does not pollute the certificate-rate denominator. Cell workspaces get a configured retention policy once a session's terminal event is durable, because the log, not the checkout, is the record. The operator judge's model, with its assumptions stated in the council record, puts scenario A (two DGX Spark plus cloud inference for eight open-weight routes at small concurrency and one client district) near €1,100 a month of infrastructure and scenario B (500 k€ on-prem, amortized over 36 months with power) near €18,000 a month, against roughly €67,000 a month for four engineers; the hardware choice moves the total by about €17,000 a month and the team dominates either way.
50	
51	### Data
52	
53	The Proving Ground already is W3's rollout mechanism; always-on operation adds continuous environment mining from Workshop failures, continuous recalibration of `EnvironmentStats`, a standing supply of certified trajectories for the SFT cold start, and a public leaderboard, not better GRPO groups. Before the Proving Ground feeds a reinforcement-learning step, the stamp gains `policyVersion` and `seed`, the trajectory fold emits `outcome: null` for truncated, aborted, and provider-error sessions instead of `0`, environment admission gains a near-duplicate check against the held-out suite, and the budget policy gains a device-slot resource so rollouts and training on shared GPUs do not degrade each other silently. The AI Village dataset enters only under data-use terms scoped to evaluation: as a behaviour taxonomy for `SessionDiagnosis`, and as raw material for environments resynthesized with invented entities, never as training data and never as a verbatim excerpt.
54	
55	### Commons and archive
56	
57	Generation zero of the archive seeds every island with more than one root so the novelty term has variance to weight; an `inconclusive` experiment verdict maps to a `parked` variant status with a configured retest cap before the variant is marked `dominated`; `ParentSample` carries sibling summaries so the quarantined Harness Engineer does not re-explore known dead ends; `LeaderboardRow` gains `harnessVariantId`; `deprecated` skills stay re-samplable when a later diagnosis names a context they were never tested in, closing only on a human rejection; and the manifest writer flags the same `KnowledgeProposal` digest appearing independently in two departments as the trigger for a portfolio-level nomination, which is how a norm like the Village's unprompted "receipt culture" would reach promotion on evidence rather than by acclamation.
58	
59	### Governance
60	
61	Five transitions never complete without a `signoff/recorded` event naming the principal and the artefact hash: spec freeze, relaxation of a security or compliance check, review acceptance, release, and training-data release; every client-district session carries `dataUse/terms` from creation; the exporter refuses to run without a redaction profile; publishing a raw excerpt is a signed decision; the EU AI Act's serious-incident channel is separate from the failure blog and routed to counsel; no training run that could approach the systemic-risk compute threshold starts before `ModelLineage` and its threshold alarm exist; and no named comparison of a competitor's model appears before the paired-experiment discipline and the isolation proof that make it verifiable.
62	
63	## Council review
64	
65	Six judges reviewed the first draft with the AI Village sources and the harness source in hand; their full reports are kept with the session's research files. Scores are out of ten.
66	
67	| Judge | Lens | Score | Decisive finding, and what changed |
68	|---|---|---|---|
69	| J1 | Software factory and client | 3 | No compliance artefact on a four-month sales clock; cost per certified session has no producer; the outreach ban was a promise. Shift zero became NDA-gated and Proving Ground only; `district` on the stamp; the composition gate; the trust dossier as the client-facing export. |
70	| J2 | Open-endedness and archives | 7 | Archive mechanics faithful to the source algorithms, but `inconclusive` had no status, generation zero had one root, and no path took emergent value to promotion. The Commons and archive section. |
71	| J3 | Reinforcement-learning data | 6 | Always-on is a scheduling wrapper around W3's mechanism; `policyVersion` and `seed` are missing from the stamp; truncated rollouts score as failures; the dataset's licence forbids training. The Data section. |
72	| J5 | Determinism and verification | 4 | The certificate does not carry its executor and an agent-reported run certifies identically; hidden checks are false for a shell-capable implementer until slice 5; tamper is the cheapest missing gate. Executor moved into slice 4 and the publication rules. |
73	| J6 | Governance and EU compliance | 3 | The draft claimed slices 1–4 and quarantine as landed; approvals carry no principal; export has no consent or redaction gate; comparative-advertising exposure. The Governance section and the status column. |
74	| J8 | Operations | 3 | Nothing above one session resumes after a crash; no shift-level budget, no circuit breaker, no retention, no durable scheduler; a cost model with stated assumptions. Shift zero's runbook and the Budgets section. |
75	
76	## Alternatives considered
77	
78	**Copy the Village format.** Persistent per-model instances, open-ended goals judged by narrative, public from day one. Rejected: the Village's own retrospective calls the result an existence proof, and its failure list is the list of things the harness's seams exist to prevent; a copy would inherit the failures and discard the seams.
79	
80	**Publish named frontier comparisons from day one.** Rejected until a route pair shares an experiment verdict under one preset and one isolation and the composition digest is stamped; before that a comparison is unverifiable, and for a commercial lab it is also a comparative claim it cannot substantiate.
81	
82	**An offline batch pipeline instead of an always-on one.** Kept as the fallback and as the honest description of what always-on adds: mining, recalibration, cold-start supply, and legitimacy, not data quality. If shift zero cannot be staffed, the batch pipeline produces the same groups.
83	
84	**One weekly cadence for every district.** Rejected for the Workshop, where a calendar reset would put a human signer under a deadline unrelated to the artefact and would force restarts on a layer that cannot yet resume.
85	
86	**Nonprofit-style disclosure of raw transcripts.** Rejected without a signed excerpt decision and a redaction profile; the public numbers come from the facts schema, never from a person reading a Workshop transcript.
87	
88	## Acceptance criteria
89	
90	- Shift zero runs the Proving Ground for seven days with every cell present as a row (report or error) and no missing sequence in the persisted logs, with a human on call and every intervention logged with a principal.
91	- The observatory shows `isolation`, executor, composition digest (or `pending`), and tamper status on every row, publishes no ranking without an `ExperimentResult` verdict, and names no frontier route before the composition digest is stamped; a snapshot test proves the withholding of Workshop and held-out sessions from the public export.
92	- `verify-village-composition` rejects a district composition without the budget policy, without persistence, or with an outreach-capable tool and no monitor, and the rejection is proven by a fixture.
93	- A certificate carries its executor; an agent-reported run cannot certify above `none`; a tamper fixture yields reward zero before any public certificate rate is published.
94	- Cost per certified session appears only once a `usage/priced` event with the pricing-table digest exists and the scorekeeper folds it; a fixture proves the same log prices identically after the table changes when the digest differs.
95	- A session derived from the AI Village dataset carries data-use terms scoped to evaluation and never appears in a training export, proven by an export fixture.
96	
97	## Rollout
98	
99	1. **Shift zero (Proving Ground, NDA).** Needs: executor on certificates (read-barrier slice 4, in progress), `district` on the stamp, the `usage/priced` event, the composition gate, cell retention, and the per-route circuit breaker; runs with a human on call.
100	2. **Public certificate rates.** Needs read-barrier slices 5 and 6 (shell denial and tamper verdicts) and the tamper column; rates then feed the archive's quality term.
101	3. **Unattended shifts.** Needs rollout item 11 of the four-goal note (idempotent cells, program ledger) and the plan-level spend aggregator; the host-level supervisor becomes a fallback.
102	4. **Named comparisons and the Commons.** Needs the composition manifest slices (digest on the stamp, preset as an experiment arm, `harnessVariantId` on the leaderboard) and the archive with `parked` and sibling summaries.
103	5. **Workshop in public and excerpt disclosure.** Needs `signoff/recorded`, `dataUse/terms`, mandatory redaction, and the trust-dossier export.
104	6. **Any outreach.** Needs the `external-communication` authority and the deny-capable monitor.
105	7. **A live observatory.** Needs the leaderboard as a cached session projection; until then the page states its batch refresh interval.
106	8. **Feeding W3.** Needs `policyVersion` and `seed` on the stamp, masked terminal reasons in the trajectory fold, near-duplicate admission, and the device-slot budget.
107	
108	## Risks
109	
110	- **A correct table under an overstated headline.** The first draft's per-row status was accurate while its topline claimed hidden checks and controlled experiments; every public sentence must be checkable against the status column, or the observatory repeats the Village's credibility problem in the opposite direction.
111	- **One missing row.** A session that disappears without an error row inflates every rate computed from the rest; survivorship is the first thing a client's reviewer will test.
112	- **Harness and model co-evolution.** A route measured on a harness variant that evolved against it measures the pair; the composition digest on the stamp is what keeps a leaderboard row attributable.
113	- **Comparative claims.** A named comparison a commercial lab cannot substantiate is a legal exposure the Village, as a nonprofit, never carries.
114	- **Sunk hardware.** Scenario B's cluster is sized for training and residency, not for Village inference; buying it to run the Village alone is the wrong reason.
115	- **Staffing dominates cost.** Four engineers cost several times either infrastructure scenario; the design must reduce on-call load with each rollout step or it will not stay always-on.
116	- **Emergent institutions.** Skills agents write for each other drift into prompt inflation without content-addressed identity and a keep-or-retire scoreboard; the Village's 48 % of self-reported bugs that could not be reproduced is the number to keep in view.

1	/**
2	 * Fleet runs: the deterministic spine of the harness capability program. A
3	 * plan of environment × model × repetition cells runs through the environment
4	 * runner, every cell's report or failure is kept in plan order, and a
5	 * leaderboard is folded from the reports without averaging across isolation
6	 * levels or the held-out split. The
7	 * [four-goal-workflows Agent Note](../../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-four-goal-workflows.md)
8	 * owns the design rationale.
9	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-fleet
10	 */
11	
12	import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto'
13	import { mkdtemp } from 'node:fs/promises'
14	import { join } from 'node:path'
15	import { Context, Service } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
16	import z from '@deepseek-ai/schemastery'
17	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-default-model'
18	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environment-runner'
19	import type { EnvironmentRunReport } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environment-runner/types'
20	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environments'
21	import type { EnvironmentDefinition, EnvironmentId, EnvironmentRunModel } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environments/types'
22	import { HarnessError } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
23	import type { FleetCell, FleetCellError, FleetCellOutcome, FleetPlan, FleetRunReport, LeaderboardRow } from './types.ts'
24	
25	export type * from './types.ts'
26	
27	declare module '@deepseek-ai/cordis' {
28	  interface Context {
29	    fleet: FleetService
30	  }
31	}
32	
33	/** Stable error codes of a refused plan. */
34	export type FleetErrorCode = 'FLEET_EMPTY_PLAN' | 'FLEET_INVALID_PLAN'
35	
36	/** Error returned by the fleet boundary for a plan that cannot run. */
37	export class FleetError extends HarnessError {
38	  /**
39	   * @param message - human-readable reason.
40	   * @param code - stable machine-routable classification.
41	   */
42	  // Keep the constructor to narrow HarnessError's string code at this boundary.
43	  // oxlint-disable-next-line typescript/no-useless-constructor -- type-only narrowing
44	  constructor(message: string, code: FleetErrorCode) {
45	    super(message, code)
46	  }
47	}
48	
49	/** Deployment choices of the fleet, validated from `cordis.yml`. */
50	export interface Config {
51	  /** Cells run at the same time; each cell is its own session and workspace. */
52	  maxConcurrent?: number
53	}
54	
55	/** The fleet's choices with every default applied. */
56	export interface ResolvedConfig {
57	  readonly maxConcurrent: number
58	}
59	
60	/**
61	 * Apply the fleet's defaults to a validated config.
62	 * @param config - validated deployment config.
63	 * @returns the resolved choices: one cell at a time unless configured.
64	 */
65	export function resolveConfig(config: Config): ResolvedConfig {
66	  return { maxConcurrent: config.maxConcurrent ?? 1 }
67	}
68	
69	/** Render a thrown value as a cell error without trusting it. */
70	function cellError(error: unknown): FleetCellError {
71	  if (error instanceof HarnessError) return { code: error.code, message: error.message }
72	  return { message: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error) }
73	}
74	
75	/** Run `tasks` with at most `limit` in flight, keeping results in task order. */
76	async function bounded<T>(tasks: readonly (() => Promise<T>)[], limit: number): Promise<T[]> {
77	  const results = new Array<T>(tasks.length)
78	  let next = 0
79	  const worker = async (): Promise<void> => {
80	    while (next < tasks.length) {
81	      const index = next
82	      next += 1
83	      results[index] = await (tasks[index] as () => Promise<T>)()
84	    }
85	  }
86	  await Promise.all(Array.from({ length: Math.min(limit, tasks.length) }, worker))
87	  return results
88	}
89	
90	/** Key of the leaderboard row a cell belongs to. */
91	function rowKey(cell: FleetCell): string {
92	  return `${cell.model.provider}�${cell.model.model}�${cell.environment}`
93	}
94	
95	/** Fold the leaderboard from the cell outcomes, one row per model route and environment. */
96	function foldLeaderboard(
97	  outcomes: readonly FleetCellOutcome[],
98	  definitions: ReadonlyMap<EnvironmentId, EnvironmentDefinition>,
99	): LeaderboardRow[] {
100	  const rows = new Map<string, LeaderboardRow>()
101	  for (const outcome of outcomes) {
102	    const key = rowKey(outcome.cell)
103	    const definition = definitions.get(outcome.cell.environment) as EnvironmentDefinition
104	    const row = rows.get(key) ?? {
105	      provider: outcome.cell.model.provider,
106	      model: outcome.cell.model.model,
107	      environmentId: outcome.cell.environment,
108	      environmentKind: definition.kind,
109	      heldOut: definition.heldOut,
110	      runs: 0,
111	      errors: 0,
112	      certified: 0,
113	      certificateRate: 0,
114	      attemptsMean: 0,
115	      inputTokens: 0,
116	      outputTokens: 0,
117	    }
118	    rows.set(key, 'report' in outcome ? withReport(row, outcome.report) : { ...row, errors: row.errors + 1 })
119	  }
120	  return [...rows.values()]
121	}
122	
123	/** Add one report to a row, recomputing the derived rates. */
124	function withReport(row: LeaderboardRow, report: EnvironmentRunReport): LeaderboardRow {
125	  const runs = row.runs + 1
126	  const certified = row.certified + (report.certified ? 1 : 0)
127	  const attempts = row.attemptsMean * row.runs + report.attempts.length
128	  return {
129	    ...row,
130	    isolation: report.stamp.isolation,
131	    runs,
132	    certified,
133	    certificateRate: certified / runs,
134	    attemptsMean: attempts / runs,
135	    inputTokens: row.inputTokens + (report.usage?.inputTokens ?? 0),
136	    outputTokens: row.outputTokens + (report.usage?.outputTokens ?? 0),
137	  }
138	}
139	
140	/**
141	 * Render a leaderboard as a Markdown table for people; the report stays the record.
142	 * @param report - a fleet run report.
143	 * @returns one table with a header row and one row per leaderboard entry.
144	 */
145	export function leaderboardMarkdown(report: FleetRunReport): string {
146	  const header = '| Model | Environment | Held out | Isolation | Runs | Errors | Certified | Rate | Attempts | Tokens in / out |'
147	  const rule = '|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|'
148	  const lines = report.leaderboard.map(row => (
149	    `| ${row.provider}/${row.model} | ${row.environmentId} | ${row.heldOut ? 'yes' : 'no'} | ${row.isolation ?? '-'} | ${row.runs} | ${row.errors} | ${row.certified} | ${row.certificateRate.toFixed(2)} | ${row.attemptsMean.toFixed(2)} | ${row.inputTokens} / ${row.outputTokens} |`
150	  ))
151	  return [`Fleet run \`${report.group}\``, '', header, rule, ...lines].join('\n') + '\n'
152	}
153	
154	/** Fleet runs (`ctx.fleet`): a plan of environment cells through the runner, with a leaderboard. */
155	export class FleetService extends Service {
156	  static inject = ['environments', 'environmentRuns', 'agentDefaultModel']
157	
158	  static Config: z<Config> = z.object({
159	    maxConcurrent: z.natural().min(1).default(1),
160	  })
161	
162	  private readonly resolved: ResolvedConfig
163	
164	  constructor(ctx: Context, config: Config) {
165	    super(ctx, 'fleet')
166	    this.resolved = resolveConfig(config)
167	  }
168	
169	  /**
170	   * Run every cell of a plan and fold the leaderboard. A cell whose run
171	   * throws is kept as an error outcome; the fleet run itself rejects only for
172	   * a plan it cannot start.
173	   * @param plan - environments, model routes, repetitions, workspace root, group, and abort signal.
174	   * @returns every cell's outcome in plan order and the leaderboard folded from the reports.
175	   * @throws {@link FleetError} when the plan selects no environment or asks for no repetition.
176	   */
177	  async run(plan: FleetPlan): Promise<FleetRunReport> {
178	    if (!Number.isInteger(plan.repetitions) || plan.repetitions < 1) {
179	      throw new FleetError(`repetitions must be a positive integer, got ${String(plan.repetitions)}`, 'FLEET_INVALID_PLAN')
180	    }
181	    const definitions = this.select(plan)
182	    if (definitions.size === 0) throw new FleetError('the plan selects no environment', 'FLEET_EMPTY_PLAN')
183	    const models = plan.models.length === 0 ? [this.defaultModel()] : plan.models
184	    const group = plan.group ?? `fleet-${randomUUID()}`
185	    const cells: FleetCell[] = []
186	    for (const environment of definitions.keys()) {
187	      for (const model of models) {
188	        for (let repetition = 0; repetition < plan.repetitions; repetition += 1) cells.push({ environment, model, repetition })
189	      }
190	    }
191	    const outcomes = await bounded(cells.map(cell => () => this.runCell(cell, plan, group)), this.resolved.maxConcurrent)
192	    return { group, cells: outcomes, leaderboard: foldLeaderboard(outcomes, definitions) }
193	  }
194	
195	  /** Resolve the plan's environment selection against the registry, in registry order. */
196	  private select(plan: FleetPlan): Map<EnvironmentId, EnvironmentDefinition> {
197	    const selected = 'ids' in plan.environments
198	      ? plan.environments.ids.flatMap((id) => {
199	        const definition = this.ctx.environments.get(id)
200	        if (definition === undefined) throw new FleetError(`environment "${id}" is not registered`, 'FLEET_INVALID_PLAN')
201	        return [definition]
202	      })
203	      : this.ctx.environments.list(plan.environments.filter)
204	    return new Map(selected.map(definition => [definition.id, definition]))
205	  }
206	
207	  /** The composition's default model route, detached from the selection service. */
208	  private defaultModel(): EnvironmentRunModel {
209	    const selection = this.ctx.agentDefaultModel.currentSelection()
210	    return { provider: selection.provider, model: selection.model }
211	  }
212	
213	  /** Run one cell in a fresh workspace directory; a thrown error becomes the cell's outcome. */
214	  private async runCell(cell: FleetCell, plan: FleetPlan, group: string): Promise<FleetCellOutcome> {
215	    try {
216	      const workspace = await mkdtemp(join(plan.workspaceRoot, 'cell-'))
217	      const report = await this.ctx.environmentRuns.run({
218	        environment: cell.environment,
219	        workspace,
220	        model: cell.model,
221	        repetition: cell.repetition,
222	        group,
223	        ...plan.signal === undefined ? {} : { signal: plan.signal },
224	      })
225	      return { cell, report }
226	    } catch (error: unknown) {
227	      return { cell, error: cellError(error) }
228	    }
229	  }
230	}
231	
232	export default FleetService

# AGENTS.md — Harness Packages

These package-specific rules supplement the repo-wide [conventions](../AGENTS.md#conventions).

- **Plugin exports:** service packages default-export their service class; function plugins named-export `name` / `inject` / `Config` / `apply` and have no default export. Mixing the forms makes the Loader discard the function plugin's namespace ([postmortem](../docs/postmortem/0001-acp-default-export-drops-inject.md)).
- **Optional services use `ctx.get(name)`.** Reserve `ctx.<name>` for declared injections; the property proxy is topology-sensitive, while strict `ctx.get` reads the global service store ([postmortem](../docs/postmortem/0001-acp-default-export-drops-inject.md)).
- **Product-visible plugins require a non-unit REAL-composition test.** Hand-built `ctx.plugin(...)` suites are insufficient. Boot test-only `cordis.yml` through the Loader and app/process; mock only external services or nondeterministic inputs and assert model-visible, durable, or user-visible output. Keep opt-ins out of shipped defaults. [Policy](../docs/testing.md).
- **Initiator-owned private chains derive, then capture.** Under `ctx.agents.withInitiator()`, recover the Agent at each orchestration entry, derive `agent.session`, and let operation-local helpers close over it. Keep `Agent` and `Session` explicit at lifecycle, session-log, service, authority, worker/process, persistence, and wire interfaces; do not widen a leaf helper from `Session` to `Context` merely to hide a parameter ([rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-15-agent-initiator-scope.md)).
- **Represent one asynchronous operation with one lifecycle controller or transaction.** Separate readiness, cancellation, disposal, reservation, or sentinel state requires an independent owner or settlement point; otherwise fold it while preserving rollback, callback containment, and quiescence.
- **Design Service Definitions for all current Consumers.** Keep tool-schema, Loader, UI, transport, and provider-specific behavior in the Consumer or provider; do not let one Consumer dictate the service contract ([capability-seam rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-06-13-capability-seams.md)). Inverse smell: a public service method with one internal caller — pass a private capability closure instead (`RunCodeBridgeOptions`).
- **Require a current owner and need.** Tie each abstraction, state machine, option, defensive copy, and compatibility path to a current contract or production consumer, and keep behavior in its owning plugin or service.
- **Require evidence for public choices.** Configurability does not justify an unsupported default, public operation set, format, or imported external concept. Use current-consumer evidence or relevant prior art; otherwise require an explicit value or defer the choice.
- **Write model-facing contracts from the model's perspective.** Prompts, tool schemas, results, and diagnostics contain only task-relevant concepts, not UI, transport, or implementation vocabulary. Pin stable model-visible text verbatim and dynamic behavior through snapshots or end-to-end coverage.
- **Enforce a decision in the operation that makes it.** Schema omission, prompt filtering, facades, wrappers, and listener order are not enforcement when direct or alternate callers can bypass them; test denial through the executor.
- **Publish state only at its commit point.** Emit each notification and update derived state only after the operation succeeds; derive caches, prompts, UI echoes, replay, and query views from one authoritative source.
- **Apply bounds to the complete result.** Enforce byte, token, item, and time limits where the complete emitted or retained value, including wrappers and metadata, is known; test tiny and exact limits, oversized single chunks, and multibyte byte limits.
- **Registry contributions prove disposal** through the HMR-safety test required by [testing policy](../docs/testing.md): dispose the fiber and observe removal.
- **Every package owns `./invariant`.** Register the manifest name; check an event/data relation or give empty installers package-specific `No runtime invariant:` reasons. Generated companions, unexplained empties, and ignored reporters fail [`verify-package-invariants`](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-19-package-invariant-runtime-contracts.md).

[Naming rules](../docs/cookbook/adding-a-package.md#name-the-role-that-exists):

- **Package tsconfig:** extends `tsconfig.base.json` (Client: `tsconfig.base.client.json`), uses `rootDir: src`, `outDir: lib/types`, and references each workspace dependency plus `runtime-diagnostics/invariants`; registers in exactly one aggregate. Only `api/remotes` splits for generated contracts; ordinary two-entry Client plugins do not ([layout](../docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- `src/types.ts` contains only types — no runtime code.
- Tests live at package level under `tests/`, not `src/__tests__/`.
- A package's README and JSDoc are part of the change: altered behavior (config keys, defaults, error codes, wire fields) updates them in the same commit. `doc-sync` gates what it can; apply [dsh-prose-standard](../.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for complete, concise prose and verify accuracy against code.
- Package READMEs document model, token, and KV-cache effects using the [canonical Model Experience format](../docs/cookbook/adding-a-package.md#4-write-the-package-readme).
- Package READMEs put durable consumer gaps and non-obvious maintainer constraints under `## Known Limitations and Deferred Work`; ordinary cleanup stays in its TODO or Agent Note. Packages with none use a justified [allowlist entry](../scripts/verify-package-readme-limitations.ts) ([rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-10-readme-known-limitations-gate.md)).

# AGENTS.md — Harness Packages

These package-specific rules supplement the repo-wide [conventions](../AGENTS.md#conventions).

- **Plugin exports:** service packages default-export their service class; function plugins named-export `name` / `inject` / `Config` / `apply` and have no default export. Mixing the forms makes the Loader discard the function plugin's namespace ([postmortem](../docs/postmortem/0001-acp-default-export-drops-inject.md)).
- **Optional services use `ctx.get(name)`.** Reserve `ctx.<name>` for declared injections; the property proxy is topology-sensitive, while strict `ctx.get` reads the global service store ([postmortem](../docs/postmortem/0001-acp-default-export-drops-inject.md)).
- **Product-visible plugins require a non-unit REAL-composition test.** Hand-built `ctx.plugin(...)` suites are insufficient. Boot test-only `cordis.yml` through the Loader and app/process; mock only external services or nondeterministic inputs and assert model-visible, durable, or user-visible output. Keep opt-ins out of shipped defaults. [Policy](../docs/testing.md).
- **Initiator-owned private chains derive, then capture.** Under `ctx.agents.withInitiator()`, recover the Agent at each orchestration entry, derive `agent.session`, and let operation-local helpers close over it. Keep `Agent` and `Session` explicit at lifecycle, session-log, service, authority, worker/process, persistence, and wire interfaces; do not widen a leaf helper from `Session` to `Context` merely to hide a parameter ([rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-15-agent-initiator-scope.md)).
- **Represent one asynchronous operation with one lifecycle controller or transaction.** Separate readiness, cancellation, disposal, reservation, or sentinel state requires an independent owner or settlement point; otherwise fold it while preserving rollback, callback containment, and quiescence.
- **Design Service Definitions for all current Consumers.** Keep tool-schema, Loader, UI, transport, and provider-specific behavior in the Consumer or provider; do not let one Consumer dictate the service contract ([capability-seam rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-06-13-capability-seams.md)). Inverse smell: a public service method with one internal caller — pass a private capability closure instead (`RunCodeBridgeOptions`).
- **Require a current owner and need.** Tie each abstraction, state machine, option, defensive copy, and compatibility path to a current contract or production consumer, and keep behavior in its owning plugin or service.
- **Require evidence for public choices.** Configurability does not justify an unsupported default, public operation set, format, or imported external concept. Use current-consumer evidence or relevant prior art; otherwise require an explicit value or defer the choice.
- **Write model-facing contracts from the model's perspective.** Prompts, tool schemas, results, and diagnostics contain only task-relevant concepts, not UI, transport, or implementation vocabulary. Pin stable model-visible text verbatim and dynamic behavior through snapshots or end-to-end coverage.
- **Enforce a decision in the operation that makes it.** Schema omission, prompt filtering, facades, wrappers, and listener order are not enforcement when direct or alternate callers can bypass them; test denial through the executor.
- **Publish state only at its commit point.** Emit each notification and update derived state only after the operation succeeds; derive caches, prompts, UI echoes, replay, and query views from one authoritative source.
- **Apply bounds to the complete result.** Enforce byte, token, item, and time limits where the complete emitted or retained value, including wrappers and metadata, is known; test tiny and exact limits, oversized single chunks, and multibyte byte limits.
- **Registry contributions prove disposal** through the HMR-safety test required by [testing policy](../docs/testing.md): dispose the fiber and observe removal.
- **Every package owns `./invariant`.** Register the manifest name; check an event/data relation or give empty installers package-specific `No runtime invariant:` reasons. Generated companions, unexplained empties, and ignored reporters fail [`verify-package-invariants`](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-19-package-invariant-runtime-contracts.md).

[Naming rules](../docs/cookbook/adding-a-package.md#name-the-role-that-exists):

- **Package tsconfig:** extends `tsconfig.base.json` (Client: `tsconfig.base.client.json`), uses `rootDir: src`, `outDir: lib/types`, and references each workspace dependency plus `runtime-diagnostics/invariants`; registers in exactly one aggregate. Only `api/remotes` splits for generated contracts; ordinary two-entry Client plugins do not ([layout](../docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- `src/types.ts` contains only types — no runtime code.
- Tests live at package level under `tests/`, not `src/__tests__/`.
- A package's README and JSDoc are part of the change: altered behavior (config keys, defaults, error codes, wire fields) updates them in the same commit. `doc-sync` gates what it can; apply [dsh-prose-standard](../.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for complete, concise prose and verify accuracy against code.
- Package READMEs document model, token, and KV-cache effects using the [canonical Model Experience format](../docs/cookbook/adding-a-package.md#4-write-the-package-readme).
- Package READMEs put durable consumer gaps and non-obvious maintainer constraints under `## Known Limitations and Deferred Work`; ordinary cleanup stays in its TODO or Agent Note. Packages with none use a justified [allowlist entry](../scripts/verify-package-readme-limitations.ts) ([rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-10-readme-known-limitations-gate.md)).

</system-reminder>

110	/**
111	 * Characters a reserved check script's path may contain. The script is sourced
112	 * as the second word of the check command line, so the path must need no shell
113	 * quoting: quoting is dialect-specific and the runner does not know the composed
114	 * shell's dialect.
115	 */
116	const UNQUOTED_COMMAND_WORD = /^[A-Za-z0-9_@%+=:,./\\-]+$/
117	
118	/** Subdirectory of a reservation holding one script per check. */
119	const CHECKS_DIR = 'checks'
120	/** Reservation file holding the standard the current attempt measures. */
121	const STANDARD_FILE = 'standard.json'
122	/** Reservation subdirectory holding a held-out environment's fixture. */
123	const FIXTURE_DIR = 'fixture'
124	
125	/** A check id usable as one path segment of its reserved script. */
126	const SAFE_CHECK_SEGMENT = /^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$/
127	
128	/**
129	 * Absolute path of one check's reserved script, refusing a check id that is not
130	 * a single path segment or a path the check command line cannot carry unquoted.
131	 * @param runDirectory - the reservation the barrier minted for this run.
132	 * @param checkId - the check's id, used verbatim as the script's file name.
133	 * @returns the absolute script path.
134	 * @throws {@link EnvironmentRunError} when the id or the resulting path is unusable.
135	 */
136	function scriptPath(runDirectory: string, checkId: string): string {
137	  if (!SAFE_CHECK_SEGMENT.test(checkId)) {
138	    throw new EnvironmentRunError(`check "${checkId}" cannot name a reserved script file`, 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_UNSAFE_CHECK_SCRIPT')
139	  }
140	  const script = join(runDirectory, CHECKS_DIR, checkId)
141	  if (!UNQUOTED_COMMAND_WORD.test(script)) {
142	    throw new EnvironmentRunError(`reserved check script "${script}" contains characters the check command line cannot carry unquoted`, 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_UNSAFE_CHECK_SCRIPT')
143	  }
144	  return script
145	}

147	/** Directory test that treats a missing or unreadable path as no directory. */
148	async function isDirectory(path: string): Promise<boolean> {
149	  try {
150	    return (await stat(path)).isDirectory()
151	  } catch {
152	    // stat rejects for a missing or unreadable path; both mean the caller named no usable directory.
153	    return false
154	  }
155	}

157	/** SHA-256 over every regular file under a directory: relative POSIX path, then bytes, in sorted order. */
158	async function hashDirectory(root: string): Promise<string> {
159	  const entries = await readdir(root, { recursive: true, withFileTypes: true })
160	  const files = entries.filter(entry => entry.isFile()).map(entry => join(entry.parentPath, entry.name)).sort()
161	  const hash = createHash('sha256')
162	  for (const file of files) {
163	    hash.update(relative(root, file).split(sep).join('/')).update('\0').update(await readFile(file)).update('\0')
164	  }
165	  return hash.digest('hex')
166	}

168	/**
169	 * Reject a workspace or fixture that is not an existing absolute directory,
170	 * then overlay the fixture and return its digest.
171	 * @returns the fixture digest, or `undefined` for a task without a fixture.
172	 */
173	async function prepareWorkspace(workspace: string, fixture: string | undefined): Promise<string | undefined> {
174	  if (!isAbsolute(workspace) || !await isDirectory(workspace)) {
175	    throw new EnvironmentRunError(`workspace "${workspace}" is not an existing absolute directory`, 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_INVALID_WORKSPACE')
176	  }
177	  if (fixture === undefined) return undefined
178	  if (!isAbsolute(fixture) || !await isDirectory(fixture)) {
179	    throw new EnvironmentRunError(`fixture "${fixture}" is not an existing absolute directory`, 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_INVALID_FIXTURE')
180	  }
181	  await cp(fixture, workspace, { recursive: true })
182	  return hashDirectory(fixture)
183	}

185	/**
186	 * Overlay the fixture again so implementer edits to validator-owned files do
187	 * not reach the checks, then digest the workspace the validation will read.
188	 * @param workspace - the run's workspace directory.
189	 * @param fixture - the task fixture, absent for a task without one.
190	 * @returns the workspace digest as the validation begins.
191	 */
192	async function restoreFixture(workspace: string, fixture: string | undefined): Promise<string> {
193	  if (fixture !== undefined) await cp(fixture, workspace, { recursive: true })
194	  return hashDirectory(workspace)
195	}

197	/**
198	 * Write the attempt's standard snapshot and one script per active check into
199	 * the reservation, so what the checks execute lives where the implementer
200	 * cannot read it.
201	 * @param runDirectory - the reservation, absent when no barrier is composed.
202	 * @param standard - the standard this attempt measures.
203	 * @returns the script path per check id; empty without a reservation.
204	 * @throws {@link EnvironmentRunError} when a check id cannot name a script file.
205	 */
206	async function materializeChecks(runDirectory: string | undefined, standard: StandardView): Promise<Map<string, string>> {
207	  const scripts = new Map<string, string>()
208	  if (runDirectory === undefined) return scripts
209	  await mkdir(join(runDirectory, CHECKS_DIR), { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 })
210	  await writeFile(join(runDirectory, STANDARD_FILE), `${JSON.stringify(standard, null, 2)}\n`, { mode: 0o600 })
211	  for (const check of standard.checks) {
212	    const script = scriptPath(runDirectory, check.id)
213	    await writeFile(script, `${check.run}\n`, { mode: 0o600 })
214	    scripts.set(check.id, script)
215	  }
216	  return scripts
217	}

219	/** Whether one executed check passed: a zero exit that neither timed out nor was aborted. */
220	function passed(result: ShellRunResult): boolean {
221	  return result.exitCode === 0 && !result.timedOut && !result.aborted
222	}
223	
224	/** Keep the first line and the tail of longer text inside the bound. */
225	function bound(text: string, maxChars: number): string {
226	  if (text.length <= maxChars) return text
227	  const newline = text.indexOf('\n')
228	  const head = newline === -1 ? text : text.slice(0, newline)
229	  const marker = '\n…'
230	  const tailBudget = maxChars - head.length - marker.length
231	  if (tailBudget <= 0) return text.slice(0, maxChars)
232	  return `${head}${marker}${text.slice(-tailBudget)}`
233	}
234	
235	/** Render one executed check's evidence: the exit fact, then the bounded output tails. */
236	function evidenceOf(result: ShellRunResult, maxChars: number): string {
237	  const exit = result.exitCode === null ? `terminated by ${result.signal ?? 'an unknown signal'}` : `exit ${result.exitCode}`
238	  const cause = result.timedOut ? ` after the ${result.timeoutMs}ms timeout` : result.aborted ? ' after the run was aborted' : ''
239	  const lines = [`${exit}${cause}`]
240	  if (result.stdout.text !== '') lines.push(`stdout: ${result.stdout.text.trimEnd()}`)
241	  if (result.stderr.text !== '') lines.push(`stderr: ${result.stderr.text.trimEnd()}`)
242	  return bound(lines.join('\n'), maxChars)
243	}
244	
245	/** One directive per failed run: the count as root cause, the evidence as detail, never the checks themselves. */
246	function describeFailures(failures: readonly CheckResult[], maxChars: number): DirectiveRequest {
247	  return {
248	    rootCause: `${failures.length} of the standard's checks failed`,
249	    detail: bound(failures.map((failure, index) => `${index + 1}. ${failure.evidence}`).join('\n'), maxChars),
250	  }
251	}
252	
253	/** The validator's follow-up turn after a failed run; the text is pinned by the runner README and its e2e. */
254	function followupText(directive: DirectiveRequest): string {
255	  return `<validation_failed>\n${directive.rootCause}\n${directive.detail}\nContinue working on the task; the validator runs again when you stop.\n</validation_failed>`
256	}
257	
258	/** Sum the usage of every assistant message in a session log. */
259	function totalUsage(events: readonly SessionEvent[]): TokenUsage | undefined {
260	  const steps = events.flatMap(event => (
261	    event.type === 'assistant/message' && event.data.usage !== undefined ? [event.data.usage] : []
262	  ))
263	  if (steps.length === 0) return undefined
264	  const total: TokenUsage = {
265	    inputTokens: steps.reduce((sum, step) => sum + step.inputTokens, 0),
266	    outputTokens: steps.reduce((sum, step) => sum + step.outputTokens, 0),
267	  }
268	  for (const key of ['cacheReadTokens', 'cacheWriteTokens', 'reasoningTokens'] as const) {
269	    const values = steps.flatMap((step) => {
270	      const value = step[key]
271	      return value === undefined ? [] : [value]
272	    })
273	    if (values.length > 0) total[key] = values.reduce((sum, value) => sum + value, 0)
274	  }
275	  return total
276	}

278	/** Environment runner (`ctx.environmentRuns`): one registered environment as one validated session. */
279	export class EnvironmentRunner extends Service {
280	  static inject = ['environments', 'agents', 'agentDefaultModel', 'goals', 'completionStandards', 'shell', 'sessions']
281	
282	  static Config: z<Config> = z.object({
283	    isolation: z.union(['none', 'process', 'host'] as const).required(),
284	    maxAttempts: z.natural().min(1).default(1),
285	    maxGoalRounds: z.natural().min(1),
286	    checkTimeoutMs: z.natural().min(1),
287	    evidenceMaxChars: z.natural().min(1).default(2000),
288	  })
289	
290	  private readonly resolved: ResolvedConfig
291	
292	  constructor(ctx: Context, config: Config) {
293	    super(ctx, 'environmentRuns')
294	    this.resolved = resolveConfig(config)
295	  }
296	
297	  /**
298	   * Run one environment as one fresh session and validate it.
299	   * @param request - environment id, absolute workspace directory, optional model route, repetition, group, and abort signal.
300	   * @returns the stamp, the attempts, the certificate when one run passed, and the accumulated usage.
301	   * @throws {@link EnvironmentRunError} for an unknown environment, an unusable
302	   *   workspace or fixture, an implementer that replaced the goal, or a lost standard.
303	   */
304	  async run(request: EnvironmentRunRequest): Promise<EnvironmentRunReport> {
305	    const definition = this.ctx.environments.get(request.environment)
306	    if (definition === undefined) {
307	      throw new EnvironmentRunError(`environment "${request.environment}" is not registered`, 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_UNKNOWN_ENVIRONMENT')
308	    }
309	    const fixtureSha256 = await prepareWorkspace(request.workspace, definition.task.fixture)
310	    const model = request.model ?? this.defaultModel()
311	    const stamp: EnvironmentRunStamp = {
312	      kind: 'environment/run',
313	      version: ENVIRONMENT_RUN_VERSION,
314	      environmentId: definition.id,
315	      environmentKind: definition.kind,
316	      heldOut: definition.heldOut,
317	      ...environmentContentHashes(definition, fixtureSha256),
318	      repetition: request.repetition ?? 0,
319	      ...request.group === undefined ? {} : { group: request.group },
320	      model,
321	      isolation: this.resolved.isolation,
322	    }
323	    const handle = await this.ctx.agents.create({
324	      sessionId: SessionId(`environment-${randomUUID()}`),
325	      meta: { cwd: request.workspace },
326	      agentOptions: { provider: model.provider, model: model.model },
327	      ...request.signal === undefined ? {} : { signal: request.signal },
328	      setup: (agentCtx) => {
329	        installModelSelection(agentCtx, { current: { provider: model.provider, model: model.model }, assembled: undefined })
330	      },
331	    })
332	    try {
333	      return await this.drive(handle.agent, definition, stamp, request)
334	    } finally {
335	      await handle.dispose()
336	    }
337	  }
338	
339	  /** The composition's default model route, detached from the selection service. */
340	  private defaultModel(): EnvironmentRunModel {
341	    const selection = this.ctx.agentDefaultModel.currentSelection()
342	    return { provider: selection.provider, model: selection.model }
343	  }
344	
345	  /** Stamp, goal, standard, then the attempt loop; the session is flushed on every path. */
346	  private async drive(
347	    agent: Agent,
348	    definition: EnvironmentDefinition,
349	    stamp: EnvironmentRunStamp,
350	    request: EnvironmentRunRequest,
351	  ): Promise<EnvironmentRunReport> {
352	    const { goals, completionStandards, sessions } = this.ctx
353	    await agent.whenIdle()
354	    const runDirectory = await this.reserve(agent, definition)
355	    agent.session.append('environment/run', stamp)
356	    const goal = goals.create(agent, {
357	      objective: definition.task.prompt,
358	      ...this.resolved.maxGoalRounds === undefined ? {} : { maxGoalRounds: this.resolved.maxGoalRounds },
359	    })
360	    goals.disarm(agent)
361	    completionStandards.author(agent, { goalId: goal.id, checks: definition.checks })
362	    const attempts: EnvironmentRunAttempt[] = []
363	    let certificate: VerificationCertificate | undefined
364	    let prompt = definition.task.prompt
365	    try {
366	      for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= this.resolved.maxAttempts; attempt += 1) {
367	        agent.followup(createUserMessage({ content: [{ type: 'text', text: prompt }], source: { kind: 'user' } }))
368	        await agent.whenIdle()
369	        const standard = this.currentStandard(agent, goal.id)
370	        const treeHash = await restoreFixture(request.workspace, definition.task.fixture)
371	        const scripts = await materializeChecks(runDirectory, standard)
372	        const results = await this.execute(standard.checks, request, scripts)
373	        attempts.push({ attempt, results, treeHash })
374	        const ref = { id: standard.id, revision: standard.revision }
375	        const outcome = completionStandards.recordRun(agent, ref, this.resolved.isolation, results, {
376	          executor: 'runner',
377	          treeHash,
378	        })
379	        if (outcome.certified) {
380	          certificate = outcome.certificate
381	          const current = goals.get(agent)
382	          if (current === undefined || current.id !== goal.id) {
383	            throw new EnvironmentRunError(`the implementer replaced goal "${goal.id}"`, 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_GOAL_REPLACED')
384	          }
385	          goals.complete(agent, { id: current.id, revision: current.revision })
386	          break
387	        }
388	        const directive = describeFailures(outcome.failures, this.resolved.evidenceMaxChars)
389	        completionStandards.issueDirective(agent, ref, directive)
390	        prompt = followupText(directive)
391	      }
392	    } finally {
393	      await sessions.flush(agent.session)
394	    }
395	    const usage = totalUsage(agent.session.events)
396	    return {
397	      environment: definition.id,
398	      sessionId: agent.id,
399	      stamp,
400	      attempts,
401	      certified: certificate !== undefined,
402	      ...certificate === undefined ? {} : { certificate },
403	      ...usage === undefined ? {} : { usage },
404	    }
405	  }

407	  /** The standard the run measures; the implementer cannot mutate it, so another goal's standard or none is an anomaly. */
408	  private currentStandard(agent: Agent, goalId: GoalId): StandardView {
409	    const standard = this.ctx.completionStandards.get(agent)
410	    if (standard === undefined || standard.goalId !== goalId) {

413	    return standard
414	  }

416	  /**
417	   * Reserve the run's validator-owned directory and stock what the checks read
418	   * from it. Without a composed barrier there is no reservation and the checks
419	   * run their instructions inline, exactly as the run's declared isolation says.
420	   * @param agent - the implementer agent this run drives.
421	   * @param definition - the environment being run, supplying the held-out fixture.
422	   * @returns the reservation, or `undefined` when no barrier is composed.
423	   */
424	  private async reserve(agent: Agent, definition: EnvironmentDefinition): Promise<string | undefined> {

426	    if (barrier === undefined) return undefined

431	    if (definition.heldOut && definition.task.fixture !== undefined) {

437	  /**
438	   * Run every active check in order through the shell executor rooted at the
439	   * workspace. A reserved check runs its script; an unreserved one runs its
440	   * instruction inline.
441	   */
442	  private async execute(
443	    checks: readonly StandardCheck[],
444	    request: EnvironmentRunRequest,
445	    scripts: ReadonlyMap<string, string>,
446	  ): Promise<CheckResult[]> {
447	    const results: CheckResult[] = []
448	    for (const check of checks) {
449	      const script = scripts.get(check.id)
450	      const spec = this.ctx.shell.resolve({
451	        command: script === undefined ? check.run : `. ${script}`,
452	        workdir: request.workspace,
453	        timeoutMs: this.resolved.checkTimeoutMs,
454	        signal: request.signal,
455	      })
456	      const result = await this.ctx.shell.run(spec)
457	      results.push({
458	        checkId: check.id,
459	        status: passed(result) ? 'pass' : 'fail',
460	        evidence: evidenceOf(result, this.resolved.evidenceMaxChars),
461	      })
462	    }
463	    return results
464	  }

37	/** Self-declared payload version of the `environment/run` event. */

40	const ISOLATIONS = new Set(['none', 'process', 'host'])
41	const HEX_64 = /^[0-9a-f]{64}$/
42	
43	/** SHA-256 hex digest of one UTF-8 string. */
44	function sha256(text: string): string {

46	}

48	/**
49	 * Content hashes of one environment: the prompt, the check inventory in
50	 * authored order, the caller-computed fixture digest, and the combined key.
51	 * @param environment - the task and checks to hash.
52	 * @param fixtureSha256 - digest of the fixture files, absent for a task without a fixture.
53	 * @returns the four digests; identical inputs give identical digests.
54	 */
55	export function environmentContentHashes(
56	  environment: Pick<EnvironmentDefinition, 'task' | 'checks'>,
57	  fixtureSha256?: string,
58	): EnvironmentContentHashes {
59	  const promptSha256 = sha256(environment.task.prompt)
60	  const checksSha256 = sha256(JSON.stringify(environment.checks.map(check => [check.id, check.outcome, check.run])))
61	  const contentSha256 = sha256([promptSha256, fixtureSha256 ?? '', checksSha256].join('\n'))
62	  return { promptSha256, checksSha256, ...fixtureSha256 === undefined ? {} : { fixtureSha256 }, contentSha256 }
63	}

65	function isRecord(value: unknown): value is Record<string, unknown> {
66	  return typeof value === 'object' && value !== null && !Array.isArray(value)
67	}
68	
69	/** Require one non-empty string field of a durable stamp. */
70	function stampText(value: Record<string, unknown>, key: string): string {
71	  const field = value[key]
72	  if (typeof field !== 'string' || field === '') throw new Error(`environment/run ${key} must be a non-empty string`)
73	  return field
74	}
75	
76	/** Require one SHA-256 hex field of a durable stamp. */
77	function stampHex(value: Record<string, unknown>, key: string): string {
78	  const field = stampText(value, key)
79	  if (!HEX_64.test(field)) throw new Error(`environment/run ${key} must be a SHA-256 hex digest`)
80	  return field
81	}

83	/**
84	 * Decode a value that declares itself as an environment run stamp. Unrelated
85	 * values return `undefined`; a malformed stamp fails replay loudly, as every
86	 * durable payload does at the log boundary.
87	 * @param value - candidate durable payload.
88	 * @returns the validated stamp, or `undefined` for another value kind.
89	 */
90	export function decodeEnvironmentRun(value: unknown): EnvironmentRunStamp | undefined {
91	  if (!isRecord(value) || value['kind'] !== 'environment/run') return undefined
92	  if (value['version'] !== ENVIRONMENT_RUN_VERSION) {
93	    throw new Error(`unsupported environment/run version ${String(value['version'])}`)
94	  }
95	  const heldOut = value['heldOut']
96	  if (typeof heldOut !== 'boolean') throw new Error('environment/run heldOut must be a boolean')
97	  const repetition = value['repetition']
98	  if (typeof repetition !== 'number' || !Number.isSafeInteger(repetition) || repetition < 0) {
99	    throw new Error('environment/run repetition must be a non-negative integer')
100	  }
101	  const model = value['model']
102	  if (!isRecord(model)) throw new Error('environment/run model must be a record')
103	  const isolation = value['isolation']
104	  if (typeof isolation !== 'string' || !ISOLATIONS.has(isolation)) {
105	    throw new Error('environment/run isolation must be none, process, or host')
106	  }
107	  const fixture = value['fixtureSha256'] === undefined ? {} : { fixtureSha256: stampHex(value, 'fixtureSha256') }
108	  const group = value['group'] === undefined ? {} : { group: stampText(value, 'group') }
109	  return {
110	    kind: 'environment/run',
111	    version: ENVIRONMENT_RUN_VERSION,
112	    environmentId: EnvironmentId(stampText(value, 'environmentId')),
113	    environmentKind: stampText(value, 'environmentKind'),
114	    heldOut,
115	    promptSha256: stampHex(value, 'promptSha256'),
116	    checksSha256: stampHex(value, 'checksSha256'),
117	    ...fixture,
118	    contentSha256: stampHex(value, 'contentSha256'),
119	    repetition,
120	    ...group,
121	    model: { provider: stampText(model, 'provider'), model: stampText(model, 'model') },
122	    isolation: isolation as EnvironmentRunStamp['isolation'],
123	  }
124	}

160	/** Copy a definition so callers never share the registry's stored check list. */
161	function detach(definition: EnvironmentDefinition): EnvironmentDefinition {
162	  return { ...definition, checks: definition.checks.map(check => ({ ...check })) }

165	/** Reject a definition whose verifiers cannot author a completion standard. */
166	function assertChecks(definition: EnvironmentDefinition): void {

172	    if (seen.has(check.id)) {
173	      throw new EnvironmentError(`environment "${definition.id}" declares check "${check.id}" twice`, 'ENVIRONMENT_DUPLICATE_CHECK')
174	    }

179	/** Environment registry (`ctx.environments`): tasks with verifiers, held at composition time. */

183	  constructor(ctx: Context) {

187	  /**

191	   * @returns the exact disposer that removes this registration and no later one under the same id.
192	   * @throws {@link EnvironmentError} when the id is already registered, the
193	   *   definition declares no checks, or two checks share an id.

195	  register(definition: EnvironmentDefinition): () => void {

198	    }
199	    assertChecks(definition)
200	    const stored = detach(definition)
201	    this.environments.set(stored.id, stored)

32	/** Render a read or fold failure for the export report without trusting the thrown value. */
33	function reasonOf(error: unknown): string {
34	  return error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)

37	/**
38	 * A sink that appends lines to one file, created or truncated on first use.
39	 * @param path - destination file path.
40	 * @returns a sink the exporter closes when the export settles.
41	 */
42	export function jsonlFileSink(path: string): TrajectorySink {
43	  const handle = open(path, 'w')
44	  return {
45	    async write(line) {

54	/** Trajectory exporter (`ctx.trajectories`): persisted sessions as training and evaluation records. */
55	export class TrajectoryService extends Service {
56	  static inject = ['sessionPersistence']
57	
58	  constructor(ctx: Context) {
59	    super(ctx, 'trajectories')
60	  }
61	
62	  /**
63	   * Fold the requested sessions and write one line per trajectory. A session
64	   * that cannot be read or folded is reported and the export continues; the
65	   * sink is closed exactly once when every session has been handled.
66	   * @param request - sessions to export, the destination sink, the reward filter, and the held-out opt-in.
67	   * @returns counts of sessions, written lines, rewarded lines, filtered sessions, withheld held-out sessions, and skips with reasons.
68	   */
69	  async export(request: TrajectoryExportRequest): Promise<TrajectoryExportReport> {
70	    const persistence = this.ctx.sessionPersistence
71	    const sessions = request.sessions ?? (await persistence.list()).map(header => header.id)
72	    const skipped: TrajectoryExportSkip[] = []
73	    let exported = 0
74	    let rewarded = 0
75	    let filtered = 0
76	    let heldOut = 0
77	    try {
78	      for (const sessionId of sessions) {
79	        let line: string
80	        let outcome: 1 | 0 | null
81	        let reserved: boolean
82	        try {
83	          const { meta, events } = await persistence.inspect(sessionId)
84	          const trajectory = foldTrajectory(meta, events)
85	          outcome = trajectory.reward.outcome
86	          reserved = trajectory.environment?.heldOut === true
87	          line = `${JSON.stringify(trajectory)}\n`
88	        } catch (error: unknown) {
89	          skipped.push({ sessionId, reason: reasonOf(error) })
90	          continue
91	        }
92	        if (reserved && request.includeHeldOut !== true) {
93	          heldOut += 1
94	          continue
95	        }
96	        if (request.rewardedOnly === true && outcome !== 1) {
97	          filtered += 1
98	          continue
99	        }
100	        await request.sink.write(line)
101	        exported += 1
102	        if (outcome === 1) rewarded += 1
103	      }
104	    } finally {
105	      await request.sink.close()
106	    }
107	    return { sessions: sessions.length, exported, rewarded, filtered, heldOut, skipped }
108	  }
109	}

111	export default TrajectoryService

1	# @deepseek-ai/dsh-fleet
2	
3	English | [中文](README.zh.md)
4	
5	Fleet runs: the deterministic spine of the harness capability program. A plan names environments, model routes, and a repetition count; the fleet runs every environment × model × repetition cell through the environment runner in its own fresh workspace, keeps every cell's report or failure in plan order, and folds a leaderboard with one row per model route and environment. Rows are never averaged across isolation levels or across the held-out split; both stay columns a consumer partitions by. The [four-goal-workflows Agent Note](../../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-four-goal-workflows.md) owns the design rationale.
6	
7	## Config
8	
9	```yaml
10	- id: environments
11	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environments'
12	- id: agent-default-model
13	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-default-model'
14	  config:
15	    provider: deepseek-official
16	    model: deepseek-v4-flash
17	- id: environment-runner
18	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environment-runner'
19	  config:
20	    isolation: none
21	- id: fleet
22	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-fleet'
23	  config:
24	    maxConcurrent: 4
25	```
26	
27	| Field | Meaning |
28	|---|---|
29	| `maxConcurrent` (default `1`) | Cells in flight at the same time; each cell is its own session and workspace directory, so the bound is a budget on agents and check processes, not on correctness. |
30	
31	The service requires `environments`, `environmentRuns`, and `agentDefaultModel`. `resolveConfig(config)` is the exported defaulting step.
32	
33	## Service contract
34	
35	`ctx.fleet.run(plan)` takes `environments` (`{ ids }` in the given order, or `{ filter }` resolved against the registry in registration order), `models` (an empty list runs the composition's default route from `agentDefaultModel`), a positive integer `repetitions`, an existing absolute `workspaceRoot`, an optional `group`, and an optional `signal`. It rejects with `FleetError` before running any cell: `FLEET_INVALID_PLAN` for a non-positive or fractional `repetitions` or an id the registry does not hold, `FLEET_EMPTY_PLAN` when the selection matches nothing.
36	
37	Cells are enumerated environment-major, then model, then repetition from `0`, and run through `ctx.environmentRuns.run` with at most `maxConcurrent` in flight. Each cell gets a fresh `cell-*` directory under `workspaceRoot` and carries the plan's `group` (or a minted `fleet-<uuid>`) and its repetition index into the run stamp, so every session of the batch is grouped durably in its own log. A cell whose run throws is kept as `{ cell, error }` with the harness error code when the error had one; the fleet run itself never fails because of one cell.
38	
39	The report carries the `group`, every cell outcome in plan order, and the `leaderboard`: per model route and environment, the environment kind and `heldOut` flag, the `isolation` the runs declared (absent when every cell of the row failed before a run), `runs`, `errors`, `certified`, `certificateRate`, `attemptsMean`, and the summed `inputTokens` and `outputTokens`. `leaderboardMarkdown(report)` renders the same rows as one Markdown table for people; the report stays the record and the session logs stay the authority.
40	
41	## Model Experience
42	
43	None, as the fleet only schedules environment runs; the environment runner owns every model-visible effect of each cell, and nothing the fleet holds enters a model request.
44	
45	#### KV Cache effect
46	
47	None; the fleet neither adds to nor changes any model request.
48	
49	## Known Limitations and Deferred Work
50	
51	- **The leaderboard is a fold of one fleet run** — cross-run comparison, paired designs across variants, and confidence intervals read the `environment/run` stamps and certificates from the session logs; this package folds only the reports it just produced.
52	- **Sampling is by repetition count** — group sampling with early stop, per-cell budgets, and retry policies are the caller's until a policy plugin exists.
53	- **Workspaces are never removed** — every `cell-*` directory stays under `workspaceRoot` for inspection; a caller that wants a clean root removes it.
54	- **A cell error carries only code and message** — the thrown error's stack and cause stay in the process, and a cell that failed before its run leaves no session; a cell that ran has every attempt as a `verification/run` event in its own session log, which is where a cross-run fold reads run evidence from.
55

1	# @deepseek-ai/dsh-trajectories
2	
3	English | [中文](README.zh.md)
4	
5	Trajectory export: persisted sessions folded into `dsh-trajectory/1` records, one JSON line each, with the chat-format message list a trainer's template consumes, the reward a certificate decided, and the components that were in play. Export reads through the session persistence seam and writes no session event. The [trajectory-export Agent Note](../../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-trajectory-export-and-environment-registry.md) owns the design rationale.
6	
7	## Config
8	
9	```yaml
10	- id: persistence
11	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-persistence-jsonl'
12	  config:
13	    root: './.sessions'
14	- id: trajectories
15	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-trajectories'
16	```
17	
18	The service takes no configuration and requires a session persistence backend.
19	
20	## Service contract
21	
22	`ctx.trajectories.export({ sessions?, sink, rewardedOnly?, includeHeldOut? })` folds each named session (or every persisted session when `sessions` is absent) through `ctx.sessionPersistence.inspect()` and writes `JSON.stringify(trajectory) + '\n'` to `sink.write()`; a session that cannot be read or folded is added to `skipped` with its reason and the export continues. A session whose `environment/run` stamp marks a held-out environment is withheld and counted as `heldOut` unless `includeHeldOut: true`, so evaluation tasks never become training data by default; `rewardedOnly: true` then withholds trajectories whose reward outcome is not `1` and counts them as `filtered`. The sink is closed exactly once, after the last write or after a failure. The report carries `sessions`, `exported`, `rewarded`, `filtered`, `heldOut`, and `skipped`. `jsonlFileSink(path)` is the shipped file sink; it truncates the file on first use.
23	
24	`foldTrajectory(meta, events)` is the pure projection behind the service and is exported for tests and offline tools. It is deterministic for the same inputs.
25	
26	## Record format `dsh-trajectory/1`
27	
28	| Field | Content |
29	|---|---|
30	| `id`, `source` | Session id; creation time, working directory, parent session, and the agent preset the log last selected |
31	| `environment` | The `environment/run` stamp the runner appended: environment id and kind, held-out flag, content hashes of prompt, fixture, and checks, repetition and group, model route, declared isolation; absent for a session no runner stamped |
32	| `config`, `system`, `tools` | Call configuration, rendered system prompt, and tool schemas of the last `request/header` |
33	| `messages` | Surface messages in model-visible order after compaction replacements: `user`, `assistant` (with `toolCalls` when requested), and `tool` (with `toolCallId`, `isError`) roles; each carries the `seq` of its source event, its `turn` and `step`, its content blocks verbatim (reasoning included), and the recorded source kind |
34	| `steps` | One entry per model call with the adapter-reported usage |
35	| `reward` | `outcome` `1` when a certificate covers the current standard revision, `0` when a standard exists without one, `null` otherwise; `basis` `certificate`, `uncertified-completion` (goal completed, no standard ever authored), or `none` (no goal); the goal snapshot, the covering certificate, and the attempt, directive, and relaxation counts |
36	| `provenance` | Component ids in the component registry's scheme (`composition:<preset>`, `environment:<id>`, `model-provider:<provider>`, `tool:<name>`), tool names in first-use order, and the certificate's isolation level |
37	
38	Token ids and logprobs are absent: the harness never sees token ids, and on-policy capture belongs to a trainer's inference proxy.
39	
40	## Model Experience
41	
42	None, as export reads persisted logs and writes files; it adds nothing to any model request.
43	
44	#### KV Cache effect
45	
46	None; the service neither adds to nor changes any model request.
47	
48	## Known Limitations and Deferred Work
49	
50	- **Off-policy text** — a trainer re-tokenizes exported text through its chat template, which suits supervised and rejection-sampled training; strict on-policy reinforcement learning needs an inference proxy in front of the harness.
51	- **No redaction** — tool results may carry credentials or private data; the sink is where a deployment applies a filter, and the telemetry redaction rules are the precedent.
52	- **One standard per session** — the reward reads the session's verification fold, which holds one completion standard; a session measuring several goals is scored by the standard in force.
53	- **No rejection-sampling export** — lines carry the environment stamp, so a consumer can group by environment, repetition, and group, but the exporter does not yet select the best of N per environment or emit per-environment statistics.
54	- **Truncation scores as failure** — a session that stopped on a token limit, an abort, or a provider error under a measured goal exports with outcome `0`; the turn-end reason is not yet a field of the record, so a trainer cannot mask it.
55
